pass_a_gloss: [...] and he shows the multitude of those who will be called, how it would be both great and countless. For your sons, he says, whom you have lost, will say into your ears: Make a place for me. And it has been said somewhere also to the spiritual Zion: Broaden the place of your tent and of your curtains, fix them. Do not spare, spread out yet into the right and the left. And we read also in the books of Moses that around the tent in the desert, I mean the one made through the skins, wide and long courts were set, some looking to dawn and ray, some also to west behind the tent, yes indeed to north and south, the type hinting at the breadth and length that will be in times of the sacred courts, or of the churches. But even so, the grace from Christ always abounding, the places are narrow for those who believed everywhere, so that also the Church rejoicing, which is spiritual Zion, reckons up and cries to herself: Who begot these for me? And I would say: the faith in Christ. For through it, being childless and a widow, you have become much in children; this reared your peoples for you, and you, once left alone, have become rich unexpectedly, and have been seen with many children, you once bare and alone. [Lemma, Isaiah 49:22-23:] Thus says the Lord: Behold I lift my hand to the nations, and to the islands I will raise my signal, and they will bring your sons in bosom, and will lift your daughters upon shoulders. And kings will be your foster-fathers, and the princesses your nurses upon the face of the earth. And they will worship you, and will lick the dust of your feet. And you will know that I am the Lord, and you will not be shamed nor turned back. Having promised to Zion that she will be of many children and of fine children, and that her children will come to this [degree] of multitude, so as also to need wider places than of old, and that she is urged to broaden the tent, he shows at once that not rather from Israel, but from the flock of the nations, the multitude of the children promised to her appears. And the thing is true, and it is possible to see it through the things themselves. For the remnant of those from Israel has been saved; but this is short and easy to count; and the [world] under heaven has been netted through faith in Christ, and the power of the apostolic and gospel preachings brought to him those throughout all the earth. That then this will be, he shows, saying: Behold I lift to the nations my hand. And the 'I lift' signifies 'I raise high' and 'I exalt'. And the hand would hint the strength, or the power. For when Christ was made known to the nations through the gospel preachings, he became high and glorious through the wonders he worked, and through the resurre[ction] [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … shows the multitude of those who will be called, how great and countless it will be. “For your sons,” he says, “whom you have lost, will say in your ears: Make room for me” (Isaiah 49:20). It is said somewhere to the spiritual Zion as well: “Enlarge the place of your tent and of your curtains; fix them firm. Do not hold back; spread out still further to the right and to the left” (Isaiah 54:2–3). We have read also in the books of Moses that around the tabernacle in the wilderness, the one made, I mean, of skins, wide and long courts were laid out, some facing the dawn and the sunrise, some to the west behind the tabernacle, and to the north and the south as well (compare Exodus 27:9–18). The figure hinted at the breadth and length that the sacred courts, that is, the churches, would have in time to come.

Yet even so, since the grace from Christ keeps on overflowing, the places everywhere are too narrow for those who have believed, so that the Church, which is the spiritual Zion, in her joy reflects and cries out within herself: “Who has begotten these for me?” (Isaiah 49:21). And I would say: faith in Christ. For through it you, who were childless and a widow, have become great in children. It has reared your peoples for you; and you who were once left alone have grown rich beyond all expectation, and have been seen with many children, you who were once bare and alone.

“Thus says the Lord: Behold, I lift up my hand to the nations, and to the islands I will raise up my signal, and they will bring your sons in their bosom, and carry your daughters on their shoulders. And kings will be your foster fathers, and princesses your nurses, on the face of the earth; and they will bow down to you and lick the dust of your feet. And you will know that I am the Lord, and you will not be ashamed or put to confusion” (Isaiah 49:22–23).

He has promised Zion that she will have many children, and fine ones, and that her children will come to such a multitude that she will need wider places than before and will be urged to enlarge her tent. Now he at once shows that the multitude of the children promised to her appears not so much from Israel as from the flock of the nations. And the thing is true, and one can see it from the events themselves. For the remnant of those from Israel has been saved, but it is small and easily counted (compare Romans 11:5); while the world under heaven has been caught in the net through faith in Christ, and the power of the apostolic and gospel preaching has brought to Him those throughout all the earth.

That this will happen, then, he makes plain by saying: “Behold, I lift up my hand to the nations” (Isaiah 49:22). “Lift up” means “raise high” and “exalt”; and the hand would suggest strength, that is, power. For when Christ was made known to the nations through the gospel preaching, He became exalted and renowned through the miracles He worked, and through the resurrection …
